He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Marquette Golden Eagles men's basketball|Marquette Golden Eagles]] and the [[Iowa State Cyclones men's basketball|Iowa State Cyclones]]. ==Early life== Deonte was born in Milwaukee, Wisconsin to Charles Burton and the late Barbara Malone. He has five brothers, Demario Burton, Omar Burton, Charles Grafton, Prentiss Grafton and Keylow Rogers and one sister Nicole Grafton.{{cite web|url=http://www.cyclones.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=8155|title=Deonte Burton – 2016–17 Basketball (M) Roster – Iowa State Athletics|website=www.cyclones.com}} After his freshman year at [[Harold S. Vincent High School|Harold S. Vincent]], and when Deonte's mother was diagnosed with cancer he transferred back to Vincent to be close to family.{{cite web|url=https://www.si.com/nba/2017/06/17/nba-draft-prospect-deonte-burton-journey|title=Pink, Poetry and Power: Deonte Burton's NBA journey|first=Jake|last=Fischer|publisher=}} After being recruited by [[Memphis Tigers men's basketball|Memphis]], [[Rutgers Scarlet Knights men's basketball|Rutgers]], and others, Burton ultimately accepted a scholarship from [[Marquette Golden Eagles men's basketball|Marquette]] to again stay close to home.{{cite web|url=http://archive.jsonline.com/sports/goldeneagles/deonte-burton-beginning-to-feel-at-home-with-mu-b99157395z1-234695241.html/|title=Deonte Burton beginning to feel at home with MU|publisher=}} {{College athlete recruit start|40=no|collapse=no|year=2013}}{{College athlete recruit entry | recruit = Deonte Burton | position = [[Forward (basketball)|F]] | hometown = [[Milwaukee, Wisconsin|Milwaukee, WI]] | highschool = [[Centennial High School (Compton, California)|Centennial High School]] (Compton, CA) [[Harold S. He averaged 6.9 points per game while earning a spot on the [[Big East Conference|Big East]] All-Rookie team. He scored a season high 23 points against [[Xavier Musketeers men's basketball|Xavier]] and scored in double figures in 13 games during the season.{{cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/deonte-burton-2.html|title=Deonte Burton College Stats - College Basketball at Sports-Reference.com|website=College Basketball at Sports-Reference.com}} ===Sophomore season=== Burton only played in eight games at Marquette before deciding to transfer.{{cite web|url=http://www.muscoop.com/index.php?topic=46024.0|title=Deonte Burton Explains Why He Transferred|website=www.muscoop.com}} During that time, he averaged 6.4 points and 40% from beyond the three-point arc. He transferred to [[Iowa State Cyclones men's basketball|Iowa State]] mid-season.{{cite web|url=http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/12058558/iowa-state-cyclones-land-marquette-golden-eagles-transfer-deonte-burton|title=Sources: Burton transferring to Iowa State|publisher=}} ===Junior season=== After transferring mid-season, Burton had to sit out the first half of the [[2015–16 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2015–16]] season becoming eligible on December 19.{{cite web|url=http://www.desmoinesregister.com/story/sports/college/iowa-state/cyclone-insider/2015/12/20/deonte-burtons-iowa-state-debut-bittersweet/77663814/|title=Deonte Burton's Iowa State debut 'bittersweet'|publisher=}} During his 26 games and seven starts, Burton had an up and down season. He averaged 9.7 points and 3.9 rebounds and was able to secure 24 steals and 16 blocks. He was also named the Big 12 Newcomer of the Year.{{cite web|url=http://scout.com/college/iowa-state/Article/Iowa-States-Deonte-Burton-Named-Big-12-Newcomer-of-the-Year-75005331|title=Iowa State's Deonte Burton Named Big 12 Newcomer of the Year|publisher=}} At the conclusion of the season Burton entered the [[2016 NBA draft|NBA draft]] for evaluation but ultimately withdrew his name.{{cite web|url=http://whotv.com/2016/05/04/cyclone-deonte-burton-withdraws-name-from-nba-draft/|title=Cyclone Deonte Burton Withdraws Name from NBA Draft|date=May 4, 2016|publisher=}} ===Senior season=== [[File:ISU vs Nevada (33342373392).jpg|thumb|right|Burton dunking the ball in the 2017 NCAA Tournament]] Burton's breakout season was his senior season. He started all 35 games for the Cyclones en route to averaging 15.1 points and 6.2 rebounds. His 60 steals tie for 16th most by a Cyclone in a single season. He scored a career high 31 points against Oklahoma.{{cite web|url=http://www.desmoinesregister.com/story/sports/college/iowa-state/basketball-mens/2017/01/21/iowa-state-oklahoma-double-overtime-deonte-burton-cyclones/96877704/|title=In double OT, Iowa State breaks recent losing run at Oklahoma|publisher=}} Burton scored 29 and hit a career best 7–9 three-pointers in a win at Kansas.{{cite web|url=https://www.ncaa.com/news/basketball-men/article/2017-02-04/college-basketball-iowa-state-upsets-no-3-kansas-home-snaps|title=College basketball: Iowa State upsets No. 3 Kansas at home, snaps 54-game streak|date=February 4, 2017|publisher=}} At the conclusion of the season He was named to the Second-team All-[[Big 12 Conference|Big 12]].{{cite web|url=http://www.big12sports.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=10410&ATCLID=211604405|title=2017 All-Big 12 Baseball Teams and Awards Announced|publisher=}} After the season he participated in the [[Reese's College All-Star Game|NABC's Reese's College All-Star]]{{cite web|url=http://www.nabc.com/NABC_Releases/2017/asg_recap|title=East Runs Past West in Reese's College All-Star Game|date=March 31, 2017|publisher=}} game and the [[Portsmouth Invitational Tournament|Portsmouth Invitational]].{{cite web|url=https://www.portsmouthinvitational.com/2017-team-rosters|title=Home – Portsmouth Invitational Tournament|website=Home – Portsmouth Invitational Tournament|access-date=July 28, 2017|archive-date=November 4, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211104154756/https://www.portsmouthinvitational.com/2017-team-rosters|url-status=dead}} ==Professional career== ===Wonju DB Promy (2017–2018)=== Burton went undrafted in the [[2017 NBA draft]], but signed with the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] for [[2017 NBA Summer League|Summer League]].{{cite web|url=http://whotv.com/2017/06/23/deonte-burton-signs-with-timberwolves-could-play-in-des-moines-next-season/|title=Deonte Burton Signs With Timberwolves, Could Play in Des Moines Next Season|date=June 23, 2017|publisher=}} He later signed with the [[Wonju DB Promy]] in [[South Korea]]'s [[Korean Basketball League]]. In Burton's single season in Korea he averaged 23.8 Points, 3.8 Assists and 7 Rebounds, which earned him the K.B.L. Foreign MVP Award.{{Cite web|title=Deonte Burton International Stats, Oklahoma City Thunder, News, Rumors, NBA Stats, NCAA Stats, G League Stats, Events Stats, Game Logs, Bests, Awards – RealGM|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/player/Deonte-Burton/International/24320|access-date=July 29, 2021|website=basketball.realgm.com}} ===Oklahoma City Thunder (2018–2020)=== Burton agreed to a two-way deal with the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] on July 7, 2018.{{Cite news|url=https://twitter.com/KeithSmithNBA/status/1015652897910976513|title=Keith Smith on Twitter|work=Twitter|access-date=July 7, 2018|language=en}} On March 10, 2019, Burton was signed to a standard NBA contract.{{cite web|title=Thunder Signs Deonte Burton to NBA Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/thunder/news/burton-190310|website=NBA.com|access-date=March 11, 2019|date=March 10, 2019}} ===Maine Celtics (2021–2022)=== On December 21, 2021, Burton was acquired by the [[Maine Celtics]] of the [[NBA G League]].{{cite web|url=https://gleague.nba.com/transactions/|website=gleague.nba.com|title=2021–22 NBA G League transactions|date=December 21, 2021|access-date=December 21, 2021}} ===Sacramento / Stockton Kings (2022–2024)=== On November 3, 2022, Burton was named to the opening night roster for the [[Stockton Kings]].{{cite web|title=Stockton Kings Announce 2022-23 Opening Night 2022}} On January 30, 2023, Burton signed a 10-day contract with the [[Sacramento Kings]].{{cite web|title=Kings Sign Deonte Burton to 10-Day Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/kings/news/kings-sign-deonte-burton-to-10-day-contract|website=NBA.com|date=January 30, 2023|access-date=January 31, 2023}} However, the Kings waived him on February 8,{{cite web|title=Kings Complete Trade With Brooklyn Nets|url=https://www.nba.com/kings/news/kings-complete-trade-with-brooklyn-nets|website=NBA.com|date=February 8, 2023|access-date=February 8, 2023}} and he was re-acquired by Stockton.{{cite web|title=22-23 NBA G League Transactions|url=https://gleague.nba.com/22-23-nba-g-league-transactions|website=NBA.com|access-date=October 2, 2023}} On October 2, 2023, Burton re-signed with Sacramento,{{cite web|title=Kings Announce 2023-24 Training Camp Roster|url=https://www.nba.com/kings/news/kings-announce-2023-24-training-camp-roster|website=NBA.com|date=October 2, 2023|access-date=October 2, 2023}} but was waived on October 12.{{cite web|first=Sam|last=Amico|title=Kings Waive Deonte Burton, Chance Comanche|url=https://hoopswire.com/kings-waive-deonte-burton-chance-comanche/|website=HoopsWire.com|date=October 12, 2023|access-date=October 12, 2023}} On November 9, he was named to the opening night roster for the [[Stockton Kings]].{{cite web|title=Stockton Kings Announce 2023-24 Opening Night Roster|url=https://stockton.gleague.nba.com/news/stockton-kings-announce-2023-24-opening-night-roster|website=NBA.com|date=November 9, 2023|access-date=November 9, 2023}} ===Mets de Guaynabo (2024)===
